SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Special Branch
REPORT.
File No. S. B. REGISTRY.
5-7
Date August 21 1934 8 34
Subject (in full).......Miss Virginia Cowper, visit to.
Made by.........D.S. Pitts.........Forwarded by.........
In compliance with the instructions of the Officer
i/c Special Branch appearing on the attached memorandum, I
have to report that Miss Virginia Cowper was interviewed on
July 31, 1934 regarding the information that she had to di-
vulge to the Police.
Actually she had no information to impart that would
be of use to this section, and the reason she solicited the
assistance of the Police was to seek advice as to what course
she should adopt regarding a Russian artist named O. Ostoya
and his wife Mrs. M. Ostoya, to whom she (Miss Cowper) had
handed a crossed cheque for $65.00 on the American-Oriental
Bank as payment for a certain painting. Apparently neither
Ostoya nor Mrs. Ostoya having banking accounts, they are ex-
periencing difficulties in cashing the cheque, with the result
that the artist and his wife accompanied by a "big, hulking,
brute of a man," have been to see Miss Cowper several times,
requesting in a threatening manner that the cheque be with-
drawn and cash issued instead. Miss Cowper alleges that
the third Russian (as mentioned above) has threatened to do
her injury, and since he is always coming in to her shop,
her business is suffering considerably.
She was advised that whilst the Police have no inter-
est in her business transactions with other persons, they
being entirely civil matters, she was at liberty to request
assistance from Central Station should any of the above men-
tioned persons return to her shop creating disturbances,
abusing or threatening her.
Officer i/c Special Branch. D. S.

档案号 S. B. REGISTRY.
5-7
日期 1934年8月21日 8 34
事由（全称）.......弗吉尼亚·考珀小姐，拜访。
制作人.........警佐 Pitts.........转呈人.........
遵照附函备忘录上特别科主管警官的指示，本人谨此报告，已于1934年7月31日约谈弗吉尼亚·考珀小姐，就其欲向警方披露的情报进行问询。
实际上，她并无任何对本部门有用的情报可提供，她寻求警方协助的原因，是就一名名为 O. Ostoya 的俄国艺术家及其妻子 M. Ostoya 夫人一事征求建议。她（考珀小姐）曾开具一张美亚银行（American-Oriental Bank）的划线支票，金额65.00美元，作为购买某幅画作的付款。显然，由于 Ostoya 和 Ostoya 夫人均无银行账户，他们在兑现支票时遇到困难，导致该艺术家与其妻子在一名“高大、魁梧、粗野的男子”陪同下，多次拜访考珀小姐，以威胁的口吻要求撤回支票并改付现金。考珀小姐声称，上述第三名俄国人曾威胁要伤害她，且因该人经常光顾她的店铺，致使她的生意受到严重影响。
已告知她，虽然警方对其与他人之间的商业交易不感兴趣，因其纯属民事事项，但若上述任何人再次回到她的店铺制造骚乱、辱骂或威胁她，她有权向中央捕房请求协助。
特别科主管警官。 D. S.

REPORT
Date Feb 25th. , 1929.
Subject (in full) Supposed Fraudulent Attempt to Collect Rent , 10, Nanking Road.
Made by D. S. I. Tinkler. Forwarded by Galway C.I.
A full report on this case has been forwarded on Crime
Report. C. 1564.
Virginia Cowper is an American lady who was formerly
employed at the American- Chinese Book Store, 25, Nanking Road.
She resides at the Astor House Hotel and her real name is Virginia
Smith-Cowper, the other name being used for her business only. She
is well known and respected in the American Community.
D. S. I.
Supt. B. Division.
W.K.
A. C. P. ( Crime ).

SHANGHAI February 21, 1929

Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
Local.

Dear Sir:

We are writing to report to you an occurance which our tenant, Miss Virginia Cowper at No. 10 Nanking Road, has reported to this office. Yesterday, February 20, two foreigners entered her shop when she seemed to be alone and demanded payment of rent. They were insistent and quite bullying in their attitude and represented themselves as the proper agents to make the collection.

It happened that there was another party in one of the corners who had not been noticed by these two and when this party stepped out to see what was going on the two men still continued their demand, but Miss Cowper ordered them promptly to leave the premises. She did not call the police as she might have done. The men then left but stood about the front of the premises for awhile, studying the name of the shop and the number, and making such remarks as, "Yes, this is No. 10", evidently ready to show that there was some mistake in their records if they had been apprehended.

We have no means of identification, but merely report this for your information.

Yours very truly,
ASIA REALTY COMPANY,
FEDERAL INC., U.S.A.
J. B. Potter

上海 1929年2月21日

警务处处长，
上海公共租界工部局，
本地。

尊敬的先生：

我方租户、南京路10号的弗吉尼亚·考珀小姐向本办事处报告了一起事件，现致函向贵处报告。昨日，即2月20日，两名外国人进入她的店铺，当时她看似独自一人，并要求支付租金。他们态度强硬且颇具欺凌性，自称是负责收租的正当代理人。

碰巧角落里有另一方人员未被这两人察觉，当此人走出来查看情况时，这两名男子仍继续其索款要求，但考珀小姐当即命令他们离开该场所。她并未像本可以那样报警。随后这些人离开了，但在店铺前逗留了一会儿，打量着店名和门牌号，并说着诸如“是的，这是10号”之类的话，显然准备表明如果被捕，他们的记录中存在某些错误。

我们没有任何身份识别线索，仅将此情况报告供贵处知悉。

此致

敬礼，
亚细亚地产公司，
美国联邦股份有限公司
J. B. Potter
